review:
Lego Ninjago The Movie is a good game with not much content. Some mechanics from the first game are removed, and some new mechanics are added. Overall, the game is fun, and typical of Lego games, funny and collectibles fest.

The changes:
1. Red Bricks in this game is replaced by 8 Ancient Scripts, there is no multiplier stud, the highest multiplier stud in this game is x2, the rest is invicibility, stud magnet, dancing step, etc.

2. No multiplier stud, how do you get lots of studs to buy things? Well, first, you dont need to buy anything in this game, each characters are unlocked after you finish certain task in the exploration or by challenging dojos. Stud multiplier can be gotten in the new battle system, which is one of the good things in this Lego Ninjago. The battle system is revamped with several flashy moves with kung-fuish names like Sky Dragon, Dancing Rabbit, etc. And each moves can have lots of combos if you do it correctly, the higher your combo, the bigger your stud multiplier will be, with max x20. 

3. Skill system, when you progress into certain parts of the story, you will get Ninjuity Tokens, you can use this tokens to unlock skills from 6 different kung-fu styles, from Dragon, Master, Rabbit, Tiger, etc. Each skills add more damage, more times to your combo, add effect to certain battle moves, etc.

4. No minikits, this can be a bummer or a blessing for some people. No minikits means, less replay value and shorter playing time, especially when the game is already short.

5. In each stage, you dont have to collect certain amounts of studs to get "True (insert something here)" status anymore, instead you will get a bar of True Ninja which represents your Ninja level, and this can be gotten from exploring the world, playing stages, or challenging dojo. Everytime you reach new leve, you will unlock body parts to be used in the character creator.

6. Dojo is another new additions in this game, each stage has one or two dojo(s) you can challenge, after clearing the dojo, you will unlock gold brick and new characters to play (new characters are unlocked if you reach the gold rank). Dojo also the fastest way to grind your True Ninja level.

7. No Free Play, after you finish a stage, you can explore all the place you visited in the stage in the open world exploration.

8. You are ninjagos, each ninjago is a master of an element, and the puzzles in this game involves using the required elements and certain character's abilities, not much changes here. 

9. No vehicles/mounts, this is one of the bad (at least for me), walking around is not cool in Lego Ninjago, but fortunately, there is a character who has the the ability to walk fast by holding B button, and you can got him in one of the dojos. 

10. I finished the game in 7 hours more or less, and got 100% in 16-17 hours. Lego Ninjago is the shortest Lego games I have ever player.

Conclusion: I recommend this game, but it doesn't worth full price guys, wait for a deep deep sale. I had fun while playing this, but it was a short fun, it's like a one night stand, fast, fun, but memorable. But in one night stand, you might unlocked the girl permanently, but this game, you won't come back to play this after you finish it.

While the LEGO Ninjago Movie didn't do so well, I really enjoyed it, and this game is equally enjoyable. It's a kids game, based on a kids movie, and when I accept that, it's much easier to love it. Of course, there's some issues with small glitches, but at the core, this game is fun. The animations are a little jagged, and maybe it's because of time constraints, but I feel like it really drives home that these are LEGO characters - tiny little action figures, running around and breaking things, collecting studs and saving the day! I love that feeling of playing with LEGOs again like an eight-year-old, kicking butts and all that. This game is great for that feeling of reliving those old days of playing with LEGOs without actually going to your parents' garage and pulling out that disorganized collection of LEGOs that you didn't bring to college. 8/10

I have very mixed feelings on this one. Seriously, it does some big things really well, and does some big things really badly.

So let's break it down:
- Con: Is yet another Lego game based on a single movie, so the story is unnaturally padded.
- Pro: Unlike with, say, The Lego Movie Videogame, this one is padded by diverging from the story, so it doesn't feel TOO much like filler.
- Con: The movie it's based on wasn't particularly good.
- Pro: The non-movie writing in the game is a whole lot better.
- Con: Uses movie cutscenes instead of proper ones.
- Pro: Outside of said cutscenes, the heavy use of Lego scenery makes it the best looking one yet.
- Con: Doesn't even line up movie cutscenes with regular game ones, so the story wouldn't even make sense if you didn't watch it first.
- Con: Ending sucked.
- Pro: Includes a lot of non-movie Ninjago stuff, such as pretty much every major character in the series.
- Pro: base gameplay was the most fun of the Lego games.
- Con: interactions are the least creative of the Lego games. There isn't a lot of "Hah, that's pretty cool".
- Pro: Postgame collectathon does not require you re-doing levels
- Con: Postgame was still pretty boring, being mostly about just trying to figure out how to get to the marked location.

...So yeah. Lots of great upsides, lots of awful downsides. Overall though, it's a voice-acted Lego game, so it's still good fun all around.

Oh, and it's a bit shorter than regular Lego games though. Just keep that in mind. My time - which includes 100% - is pretty abnormally fast though, but that's because I played at 2x speed.

Overall, I would say that this game was good, not great. Being the 12th Lego game that I've replayed this year (and despite my constant love for Ninjago as a TV show) this one doesn't quite hold a candle to a lot of the other games in the TT/Lego Franchise. 

That being said, I would be a liar if I said I had no fun at all playing this one. The character roster is great, the dojos are super fun to go through, and while the levels are relatively short, they're good for what they are. I think I honestly just wish that they based this game off of the TV show instead of making references to it. The show (in my opinion) has much more depth, nuance, and cool worldbuilding than the movie had/could ever have. Despite all of that, some of Garmadon's lines did make me actually laugh out loud as I played this. 

All in all, I would say to pick this one up at a discounted if you're a completionist (like me) or a superfan of the Ninjago series. Otherwise, I would to say to spend your hard earned cash on a better Lego game :D

The price made me hesistant to buy but I wanted a game to play with my son. Because of the poor quality of video and audio in the trailer I was worried that this game would be a effortless cash grab. After a few hours I am happy to say that this is one of the best Lego games I've ever played. It runs smooth as butter except for a few glitches including ctd and freezing. Split screen is verticle which makes me feel like I'm veiwing the game through a key hole. Cut scenes from the movie are jittery and cut mid sentence. First off, I wasn't impressed with the movie when I saw it. Second, I tried a season of the original TV show. That actually wasn't too bad.

So when it came to this game not being faithful to the movie (i.e. different voice actors / music and skipping along through the plot, spending very little time in the Mechs) none of that bothered me, because they weren't parts of the movie I was desperate to experience.  Things that they added from the show (i.e. mostly extra collectible characters and some version of spinjitzu and tornado of creation) were delightful inclusions.

But what I enjoyed the most about this game were the things that made it stand out from the other LEGO games. 

The slightly more complex combat mechanics, of course, were a nice touch: more than just punch punch punch but not so much that it would be hard for a kid to perform the combos. Though, I think I liked the pre-ninjanuity tokens combat better. Those tokens tended to make enemies die faster and thus your combo wouldn't get as big.

The fact that the hub worlds ARE the levels I thought was a really good idea. Often the open/hub worlds can feel very separated from the main story, so having them be the same maps made it all feel connected. 

The Dojo's were great! If you want more goons to fight at once, that's what the Dojo's are going to provide you. I could build up a decent combo and collect loads of studs! 

The arena is great for multiplayer combat ... I assume. It looked like traditional CTF sort of stuff, and if you love multiplayer, you'll probably have at least a bit of fun. It's not my thing, but the point is they added varied game play, which always helps break up the monotony. So it's a plus.

I thought getting characters in minifig bags was a nice change from purchasing them. I never liked spending my hard earned studs on characters in the other games. I'd never buy any until I had most of the stud multipliers, so it'd basically be the last thing I'd do and thus I'd never have fun with new characters. So this is much more fun. And I appreciate that when looking at all the characters, the user interface can highlight all the characters with a specific ability. That made me more likely to vary up who I played as, since i could tell who did what.

Overall, I think this was a PHENOMENAL edition to the LEGO video game franchise. If you're worried about it not being fun, don't. It's fun. If you're worried it won't live up to the legend that is Ninjago, well I can't tell you how you'll feel. You'll either be bummed out by little differences or you'll enjoy it despite the differences. For me, this game definitely Exceeded My Expectations!

I think LEGO games are ultimately the best when they are an original LEGO theme, rather than the DC/Marvel/WB IPs. I don't really know what it is about this game, but it really feels like they put a lot of heart into it compared to the other recent titles. The characters are animated on a different framerate than the rest of the world, which makes it feel very LEGO-ey. There's neat little combat options - ultimately, it's just button mashing like before, but it makes it feel cool when there's a combo meter, and there's even upgrades to that combat system that get unlocked as the story progresses. They did away with level-based True Jedi-type progress, and actually instead opted for eight fairly expansive levels for the collectibles - plus, the free roam doesn't force you to replay the story, they just have another option for that, which is a real QoL improvement. I REALLY like that the game actually forces you to look around and explore, rather than having a flying character to trivialize gathering all of the collectibles. Obviously, it's not gonna do that much for someone that doesn't know anything about Ninjago, but I think that this is definitely one of the more solid LEGO games put out :)

I played this game for about 4.1 hours and finished the main story. No 100%, no side content—just a casual playthrough to see what it’s like after picking it up on a heavy discount.

Story

The story is basically just the movie. And I mean literally.

Instead of properly adapting it, the game uses actual movie footage mixed with in-game cutscenes, and the transitions between them are really bad. It feels disjointed and awkward, like it cuts in the middle of scenes and then jumps into gameplay.

Because of that, the story feels pointless. There’s no real reason for this to exist as a game. It would have been much better if they created an original story instead of just copying the movie.

Gameplay & Combat

This is easily the best part of the game.

The combat system is the best I’ve seen in a LEGO game so far
Combos are fun and more engaging than usual
It actually feels like they tried to evolve the gameplay

However:

There is noticeable input delay / responsiveness issues
The game feels restricted early on because you don’t have full abilities
It takes almost the entire game (around 90–95%) to unlock everything, which hurts the pacing badly

The puzzles are decent, but limited early on due to lack of abilities. Once everything opens up, it gets better—but by then, you’re basically done with the game.

Characters

The characters are exactly what you’d expect from the movie/show versions.

They’re fine, but nothing particularly special in this game
Lord Garmadon stands out the most
Kai is good here, but compared to the original show, he feels less like a strong leader and more toned down

The movie versions and show versions are slightly different, and personally, I prefer the show’s characterization more.

Level Design

This is another strong point.

Environments look great
Levels are visually interesting
Fun to move through, even if you’re not exploring deeply

I didn’t spend much time exploring, but from what I saw, the world design itself is solid.

Humor & Tone

The humor is actually decent compared to other LEGO games.

Not laugh-out-loud funny
But definitely better than some other entries
Works well for kids especially
Technical
No crashes or major bugs
Graphics are good for a 2017 LEGO game
Sound design is solid

Main issue:

Noticeable input delay during gameplay, especially in combat
Final Thoughts

I didn’t really enjoy finishing this game.

If I went back in time, I probably wouldn’t buy it again—even on sale. The gameplay shows real potential, especially the combat system, but everything else feels like a lazy movie tie-in.

Recommendation
If you’re a Ninjago fan: You might enjoy it
If you just like LEGO games: Only get it on a deep sale
Otherwise: It’s very skippable
Score
Full Price: 0/10
On Sale: 4/10 (carried almost entirely by the combat)

Another Lego game, and another game based off of a movie. And this one is pretty good all things considered. I'll be listing off various things about this game that I liked/ didn't like, and the features that it does and doesn't have, so chances are I'll hopefully answer any questions one may have about this game before buying it. So let's begin.

The story: If you've seen the movie, you've pretty much seen the game. It even uses clips from the movie in place of cutscenes, which works to some degree but I'll touch on that later. As such, the main story follows that of the film, and while it does leave some things out, it also places a lot in. For instance, you get a lot more character with Jay when you play as him and Lloyd in the second act. And it makes the film just a little bit weaker in comparison, and I kinda like that, as I mentioned before, it gives him a bit more character. There are other scenes like that, but sadly not many.

Voice work: I'll be honest when I say I really don't know to much about this department, and have never really reviewed it before, but if you're expecting Michael Pena to be voicing Kai in this, then you're gonna be dissapointed, because as far as I know, none of the voice actors from the film appear in this game. The actors that do appear in this game try their best to imitate their film portyals and of which they do to a certain extent. You can clearly see (hear?) this in Garmadon, whenever he say's La-Loyd. It just doesn't feel right, and the fact that they're using clips from the actual film and having these actors "dub" over it just feels wrong. And after seeing the movie (twice) and then playing the game and recalling how the voices should sound, it just feels like a piece was missing from the instructions. (I'm sorry, I had to make a pun.) Regardless of who is voicing them though, they still do an alright job pulling off the characters and making them enjoyable to play as. Also don't expect anyone to say anything when in free-roam, that's been left out sadly.

 Controls: If you've played past Lego titles on the PC, then this one should really feel no different. Keys are awkward and layout is pretty much the same. If you use a controller (XBox like I do) then you'll probably have a much better time with this game. Some mechanics from past Lego games have been implemented such as the dodge ability (RT and LT on a controller) that allow you to evade enemy attacks and instead of pre-determined moves like in Avengers, you now have several attack styles to use, such as the Rushing Boar (tap X on controller and use L-thumbstick towards an enemy) and the Skyward Dragon, which allow you to raise your combo meter even higher than in past games. And the more you raise your meter, then bigger multiplier for studs you'll get. The place you really see this come to frutition is in the arenas, which I'll talk about later.

Levels: I could've talked about this when talking about the story, but it didn't fit in in any way that felt right, so I decided to just make it a seperate topic. Reason is is because in truth, there are no levels. And by that, I mean there are no story-exlusive stages where you're dragged out of the map, and placed into a different one. The chapter you play is also the map you play on. Kinda like Assassin's Creed. And what this does is it effectlivly makes the environment you play in much more memorable, which is kinda neat in a way, esspecially with the Docks. The big downside to this, and one that might hurt some opinions on the game, is that there are no longer any Mini-kits or True-___ collectibles. (i.e. True Jedi for Lego Star Wars) In place of the True-___ stud meter is a simple level up bar that fills up with the Lego studs that you collect, and while still called True-Ninja bar, it only serves as a level up gauge that once leveled up, unlocks some customization parts. There are no replacements for the Mini-kits, which has been a long time staple for the Lego games, but given how they made the actual maps the levels themselves, I can kinda see why they did it. Apart from that though, there really is no limit to what you can do inside of a story mode mission so long as you have the right character. Granted you can't accept side-quests while in a story because you can't, but you can go out of your way in the story to collect a Gold Brick, pick up Red Brick, or even snatch up a mini-figure bag (Yes, bag. They're like blind bags now and it's really cool.) And mind that everything you unlock is free, which kinda negates having a True-Ninja bar in the first place. The only things studs are used for are for Tornado of Creation Builds, which do cost a shiney stud when first playing, but other than that, you don't use studs at all. There are some side-levels, called Dojo's, where you'll be required to gain a certain amount of studs to unlock all 3 characters, but those are pretty easy to get. The Dojo's themselves are also pretty nice, taking place outside of the map in a themed area and have you going up against some of the show's main villians.

Graphics: It's a Lego game. They look like Legos. But the game does look really good, blending Legos and real-world environments to make it believable.

 Arenas: Basically the multiplayer part of the game aside from normal 2-player co-op, Arenas do what Battle Mode did back in the day of Lego Star Wars: The Complete Saga. Only now it can hold up to four players. And while there are only 3 modes, Samurai Showdown, Mystic Bounty, and Ulitmate Ultimate Weapon. Samurai is basically capture the flag, and the more flags you hold, the slower you go until you can get them to your base. Mystic is an orb collecting mode, with various orbs scattered throughout the map that vary in points. UUW is where you hold onto the UUW and earn points. Whoever holds onto it the longest wins. For all games, it's really who gets the most points wins, and they're fairly easy, against the ai bots that is. At the moment, there are only 3 maps, and I don't know if there will be more for I don't even know if there will be dlc for this game. But the maps are based in Ninjago City, the Uncrossable Jungle, and the Unclimbable Mountain, each being the same in each mode. There are also items that can be used to your advantage in each, but none are exclusive to a map, Now these modes are most definatly fun, as I find myself going back to them just to see what I can do, and I would totally like to see this area be expanded upon should there be dlc released.

Character List: Probably the only other disapointing thing about this game is the lack of characters. While it does feature main characters from the show such as Kai in his Season 2 outfit and Pythor, it only features just about one of each character, which is a shame because of all the great outfits that the Ninja wore throughout the seasons along with upgraded color schemes that some villians got as well. At present, there are a total of 101 characters, not including the custom ones, and a locked character that has yet to be revealed, even at 100%. And there are some characters that I would have loved to play as such as Season 5 Cole in his Ghost form, or the Titanium Ninja, and some characters such as Classic Zane and Cole could've really benifitted from using their classic weapons instead of their movie counterparts gear. It's another Lego game and if you have played any of the other Marvel, Batman or Lego Movie games there isn't much here that will surprise you.  For the most part it follows the same path that the other games take.  You start off with a small collection of Characters as you work through some levels and unlock more characters with different abilities/powers to go back through the levels and complete more of the challenges to access more characters.  There is a few differences that this game takes compared to the other ones, those differences though were not exactly positive.

The level design was well done in here, there is a good deal to explore in the levels and makes good use of the space in the level to put in some fairly easy challenges (it is supposed to be a kids game).  The length of each level was fine as well, none of them felt overly long or to short.  

The game controls about as well as any other Lego game, I always recommend a controller for these games, they just feel better with one, though K+M works as well.  The only control issue I had was there was sections where you were expected to push one button to make jumps to small platforms, for whatever reason it didn't work like it should and the character would fall to their deaths instead of make the jump, while at other times it worked flawlessly, not sure what was going on there but it was a little annoying.

In previous Lego games you collect Lego studs as a form of currency, in this game you still collect it but not longer works as a form of currency to unlock characters like previous Lego games.  In this game as you collect the studs you will get to check points that will reward you with some pieces for making a custom character, so collecting those felt a lot less useful this game.

A fighting combo system was added to this game for battle that allows you to build up a large chain of attacks to give you a x2, x4, x6, x8, etc.... on your stud collection to help with the previous point.  It doesn't add a whole lot but it does make some of the 'boss' battles a little more interesting.  I still didn't find the boss battles that exciting compared to the marvel/batman lego games but I think it kind of fits with the world this game is set it.

The game isn't overly long, the amount of time I put in was enough to 100% the game outside of the battle arena.  Those who like some local area co-op or battle arena may be able to put in a lot more time.

There also is no large hub area's like Lego Marvel Super Heroes, which is disappointing.  You get the 8 levels or so you can switch between, but there is not one large area you can just have fun in with all the unlocked characters.

Overall its a Lego game, you know what you are going to get if you've played some of the others, it's not as good as the marvel versions of Lego games, but it's also not a bad game.  Would recommend getting it on sale if you are just interested in the campaign as it doesn't take much to 100% the game.

A very monotonous experience. The gameplay doesn't offer anything interesting or engaging, making it feel like it's always on auto pilot. Considering this is a LEGO game we're talking about here that's not saying much. I'm personally a big fan of this series but I didn't even bother finishing it due to bored I got by the final level. TT Games tries to implement parkour and combat mechanics into their stagnant LEGO game formula here but it never offers any interesting platforming challenges or puzzles. Everything can be completed with a couple presses of a button with no skill required making the gameplay unengaging. Even though you have more combat abilities to play around with than in previous entries the combat still feels just as mindless as any other LEGO game. There's a good variety of stuff to find (Gold Bricks, Unlockable Characters, etc.) as you explore the variety of small environments in the game, but I had no motivation to collect anything since the majority of characters you find are uninteresting extras from the movie and with the gameplay being as bland as it is I couldn't find the motivation to go back in free play to find everything. Considering the source material this game had a lot of potential but it never capitalizes on it and ends up feeling like a half baked movie adaptation rather than a Ninjago videogame. (i.e. Spinjtizu functions as a glorified projectile attack that is used for very shallow puzzles and isn't fun to use in combat.) I didn't like the LEGO Ninjago Movie to begin with (I am more of a fan of the Masters of Spinjitzu TV show bc of nostalgia) so the story here is still as bad and is even worse due to how they try to awkwardly combine in game cutscenes with the movie. All of the in-game voice acting is cringe inducing and the humor is even worse. (No Zane I don't care that you're a robot who says "LOL" unironically... shut the hell up please.) The presentation is solid for the most part. I like how this game looks despite some of the set pieces looking a little stiff and me not being a big fan of the movie's aesthetic. There are some good ideas here scattered about but nothing amazing. This is essentially just another LEGO game with a Ninjago Movie flavor. If you're beginning to get tired of this formula like I am avoid this one and spend time playing something with more thought put into its design.

  Now this wouldn't be an honest review if I didn't mention the bad side of the game, the bugs and the part that I didn't like personally. LEGO Ninjago: 7/10

Originally, I gave this game a 4/10, but after reflecting on it, I think a 7/10 is much more fair.

My biggest issue with this game was how frequently it crashed. It got incredibly frustrating, especially when I just wanted to sit down and enjoy the game. The story also felt very linear, and at times, it got pretty boring.

However, I absolutely love Ninjago, and that definitely plays a big part in my enjoyment of this game. Getting to play as all these different characters was so cool, and the combat was honestly amazing. It was one of my favorite aspects of the entire experience.

Honestly, I would love to see another LEGO Ninjago game based on the earlier seasons of the show. There is so much potential there, and this game reminded me how much I the Ninjago universe.

Overall, the crashes and linear story hold the game back, but the fantastic combat, character roster, and my love for Ninjago make this a much better experience than my original 4/10 rating suggests. 7/10.
